src.utils package

This package contains utility modules and shared helper functions that are used throughout the project.

It provides reusable components such as ai image generating, file handling, image processing, configuration loading, slicing utilities, and communication helpers to support the core functionality of the application.

src.utils.ai_helper module

This module handles all processes related to the image generating using different AI models.

It executes image generating in a separate process, and provides CRUD operations for AI Settings stored in a SQLite database.

Classes:

AIHelper: Main helper class to manage AI image generation and settings workflows.

Functions:

generate_images: Worker function executed in a separate process to perform the AI image generating procedure.

Runs an external image generation subprocess with provided AI settings.

src.utils.default_materials_data module

class utils.default_materials_data.DefaultMaterialsData

Bases: object

Provides default data insertion into the database for materials, thicknesses, operations, and engraving settings.

This class is typically used to populate the materials-related tables with default values during the initial database setup.

static add_default_data(cursor)

Inserts default values into the database if they do not already exist.

Tables affected:

  • Materials

  • Thicknesses

  • Operations

  • Engraving_Settings

Each INSERT OR IGNORE statement ensures that default data is not duplicated if it already exists.

The inserted data defines:

  • One default material

  • Three thickness levels for that material

  • Three types of operations (Cut, Mark, Engrave) per thickness

  • One engraving setting per Engrave operation

Parameters:

cursor (sqlite3.Cursor) – The database cursor used to execute SQL insert statements.

src.utils.job_execution_timer module

class utils.job_execution_timer.JobExecutionTimer

Bases: object

Tracks the execution time of a job with support for start, pause, resume, stop, and reset.

This timer allows measurement of active execution time by managing paused durations. Useful for tracking how long a file/job has been executing, excluding paused intervals.

_start_time

The time when the job start getting executed.

Type:

float

_pause_time

The time when the job execution get paused.

Type:

float

_paused_duration

How much time the job got paused (Duration of pausing the job)

Type:

float

_is_running

flag for the job execution process.

Type:

bool

get_elapsed_time()

Gets the total elapsed time in seconds, excluding paused durations.

Returns:

The elapsed execution time in seconds.

Return type:

float

pause()

Pauses the timer.

Records the time when the pause started.

reset()

Resets the timer to its initial state.

Clears all timing values and stops the timer.

resume()

Resumes the timer from where it was paused.

Adjusts the paused duration so it’s not counted in elapsed time.

start()

Starts the timer.

If the timer was previously paused, it resumes from where it left off.

stop()

Stops the timer without resetting its values.

Useful when you want to finalize tracking but keep time info available.

src.utils.priority_queue_with_counter module

class utils.priority_queue_with_counter.PriorityQueueWithCounter

Bases: object

A custom priority queue that maintains insertion order for items with the same priority.

This class wraps around Python’s built-in PriorityQueue and adds a counter to ensure FIFO behavior for items with identical priorities. It is designed to work well with multiprocessing-safe managers (SyncManager) where shared data structures require thread-safe communication between processes.

Each item put into the queue includes:

  • priority (int): Lower values indicate higher priority.

  • counter (int): Incremental value to preserve insertion order among same-priority items.

  • type (str): A label or identifier for the item.

  • item (optional): The actual data or payload associated with the queue entry.

_priority_queue
Type:

PriorityQueue

_entry_counter
Type:

int

empty()

Checks whether the queue is empty.

Returns:

True if queue is empty, False otherwise.

Return type:

bool

get()

Removes and returns the next item in the queue based on priority and insertion order.

Returns:

(type, item) of the dequeued entry.

Return type:

tuple

put(type, priority, item=None)

Adds an item to the queue with a given priority.

Parameters:

  • type (str) – Identifier or label for the item.

  • priority (int) – Lower values represent higher priority (e.g., 1 is higher than 2).

  • item (str, optional) – Actual data to enqueue. Defaults to None.

src.utils.shared_data module

This module manages shared memory structures across multiple processes using Python’s multiprocessing.managers.SyncManager. It defines classes to initialize and access shared queues, flags, and counters for use between core services such as serial control, websocket communication, FastAPI, and camera systems.

It ensures safe inter-process communication using manager-backed data types like queues and shared values.

Classes:

  • SharedDataManager: Starts the shared manager and registers custom types.

  • SharedMachineData: Stores shared queues and flags for machine connection process.

  • SharedWebsocketData: Manages shared queues and execution flags for WebSocket connection process.

  • SharedFastApiData: Provides read/write queues for FastAPI communication.

  • SharedCamerasSystemData: Provides read/write queues for camera stream data handling.
